greek.forms: Singular: ἀρετή, ἀρετῆς, ἀρετῇ, ἀρετήν; Plural: ἀρεταί, ἀρετῶν, ἀρεταῖς, ἀρετάς
greek.etymology: Root: ἄριστος (aristos) = "best". English descendants: Aristocracy (rule by the best/nobles), Aristocrat (member of the nobility), Arete (philosophical term for virtue), Aristeia (moment of glory in epic poetry). All derive from the concept of excellence or being the best.
greek.usage_example: ἡ ἀρετὴ ἕξις προαιρετικὴ ἐν μεσότητι οὖσα — Excellence is a deliberate disposition lying in a mean.
greek.did_you_know: Ancient Greeks had different words for different types of excellence: ἀρετή for moral virtue, τέχνη for skill-based excellence, and ἀριστεία for battlefield heroics. Athletes could win prizes for ἀρετή in character, not just performance!
